headline: KOREA SHIPPED
**$70B** OF ICT
cover.hook_pick_reason: The $70B hook puts the biggest figure first and slides 1 to 5 back it: ICT exports of $70.35B in October, second-highest month ever, led by chips. The 61% hook is accurate but less vivid, the 259.4% hook covers only semiconductors, and the tripled hook leans on the AI link, which the article gives as demand for memory and high prices. No reader-impact hook: the article reports Korean trade data and states no effect on what ordinary readers pay, use or risk.

slides.title: ICT exports more than tripled
body: South Korea shipped **$70.35B** of ICT (information and communications technology) products abroad in October, up from **$23.29B** a year earlier. The data comes from the Ministry of Science and ICT.

slides.title: Over 60% for three months
body: October was the **second-highest month on record**, just below September's $75.1B. ICT made up **61%** of Korea's total exports of $115.28B, staying above 60% for three straight months.

slides.title: Semiconductors led the surge
body: Chip exports jumped **259.4%** from a year earlier to **$56.47B**. The article credits strong global demand for premium memory products and persistently high memory prices.

slides.title: Server drives and phones
body: Computers and accessories reached **$5.99B**, more than fivefold, led by high-capacity solid-state drives (SSDs) for servers. Mobile phones rose a modest 6.5% to $1.71B on premium models.

slides.title: China and the US
body: Exports to **China** more than tripled to $27.2B, driven by chips and computers. Shipments to the **United States** grew more than sixfold to $15.56B.

sources.title: ICT exports log record-high growth in Oct. amid AI boom

facts.text: Outbound shipments of ICT products came to $70.35 billion in October, more than tripling from $23.29 billion a year earlier, according to data compiled by the Ministry of Science and ICT.
The figure marked the second-highest monthly total on record, just below the $75.1 billion posted in September.
ICT exports accounted for 61 percent of the country's total outbound shipments of $115.28 billion in October, with the proportion remaining above 60 percent for three consecutive months.
Exports of semiconductors shot up 259.4 percent on-year in October to $56.47 billion, driven by strong global demand for premium memory products and persistently high memory prices.
Outbound shipments of computers and accessories reached $5.99 billion in October, growing more than fivefold from a year earlier, led by high-capacity solid-state drives (SSDs) for servers.
Exports of mobile phones rose 6.5 percent to $1.71 billion on the back of strong sales of premium models.
Exports to China more than tripled to $27.2 billion, driven by gains in semiconductors and computers. Shipments to the United States grew more than sixfold to $15.56 billion.
